findings.title: Google credential key stored as safeParse result wrapper
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a zod SafeParseReturnType of the form {success, data}. Here it is used directly as `key` and saved to the DB. Previously the code saved googleCredentialSchema.parse output, i.e. the token object itself. After the first refresh the stored key becomes {success, data}, which breaks googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key) on the next load and disables the calendar.

findings.title: Sync endpoint Response has no .data
findings.body: When credential sync is enabled, refreshOAuthTokens returns a raw fetch Response. This code reads `res?.data` as if it were a gaxios response. A fetch Response has no `.data`, so `token` is undefined and `token.access_token` throws. Google token refresh is always broken in sync mode. The same mismatch affects hubspot (expects a token object), zoho-bigin and zohocrm (expect an axios `.data`).

findings.title: prisma used without import; refresh on every construction
findings.body: `prisma` is referenced but never imported in this file, so it is undefined and getClient throws a ReferenceError at runtime. Separately, the token is refreshed on every service instantiation. Even after refreshing, the jsforce Connection is still built with the old credentialKey.access_token rather than the new one.

findings.title: credentialId passed as userId
findings.body: refreshOAuthTokens expects a userId, but this call passes credentialId. The sync endpoint is therefore asked for tokens belonging to the wrong user, which can leak another user's tokens or return the wrong account's tokens.

findings.title: Wrong app slug 'zoomvideo'
findings.body: The app slug for Zoom is "zoom", as used in callback.ts and on credential.appId. Sending "zoomvideo" to the sync endpoint means the self-hosted side will not match the app.

findings.title: Non-constant-time secret compare; unhandled parse errors
findings.body: The webhook secret is compared with `!==`, which is not constant-time and is open to timing attacks; use timingSafeEqual. There is also no HTTP method check. zod `.parse` and JSON.parse/decrypt failures are not caught, so bad input produces 500 errors instead of 400s.

findings.title: Bogus zod schema keys and fake refresh_token
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` evaluates to the literal key "[object Object]", so the schema actually requires a property literally named that. With both computed keys collapsing to that one name, the last entry wins and it ends up optional unknown, so the expiry check is not enforced at all. Also, a missing refresh_token is replaced with the placeholder string "refresh_token" and persisted, which corrupts stored credentials outside sync mode.

findings.title: Refresh failures now throw instead of logging
findings.body: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on an invalid response. The previous code merged what it could and logged the zod error and the Microsoft response. That diagnostic logging has been removed, and the `tokenResponse.success &&` check on the next line is now dead code.

findings.title: Hardcoded redirect slug mismatches callback
findings.body: add.ts now hardcodes "zoho-bigin" in the redirect URI, while callback.ts still builds it from appConfig.slug. If the two values ever differ, the OAuth token exchange fails because the redirect_uri does not match.
